Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Higher serum 25(OH)D levels were associated with lower depressive symptom severity (K-HDRS) in women with secondary amenorrhea, after adjusting for age and BMI.
Sentence: "The total score of the Korean version of the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (K-HDRS) was negatively related to serum 25(OH)D levels, free testosterone, and serum anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) after adjusting for age and BMI (r = −0.450, p < 0.001; r = −0.258, p = 0.045; and r = −0.339, p = 0.006, respectively)."
Measured as: depressive severity (K-HDRS total score)
Population: Korean women with secondary amenorrhea (63 analyzed of 78 recruited)
Intervention: Serum 25(OH)D level (observational exposure, no intervention)
Comparator: None; association across participants
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 78
baseline_vitamin_d_status: mixed

## Study B
Found: harm
Claim: In PD patients given vitamin D3, folic acid and B12 for 6 months, the 15D depression dimension score significantly increased (improved) from baseline.
Sentence: "After the intervention, the mean score of speech, mental function, discomfort and symptoms, depression, and QoL significantly increased (p < 0.05 for all)."
Measured as: depression (15D dimension score)
Population: Levodopa-treated Parkinson's disease patients in Romania, mean age 71 years
Intervention: Daily tablet with 800 IU vitamin D3, 1000 µg folic acid, 15 µg vitamin B12 for 6 months
Comparator: None (single-arm, baseline vs 6 months)
Design: case series
Sample size: not reported
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

  "rationale": "Both studies actually found a benefit for depression, as Study B measured the 15D depression dimension where a higher score means improvement rather than harm, and rated depression as a single item on a general quality-of-life questionnaire rather than a full depression scale.",
